dedupe_keys.name: tides transit its data exchange specification for historical transit operations data avl apc fare transactions

description: TIDES, the Transit ITS Data Exchange Specification, is an open data standard for the historical operations data that transit agencies collect from their intelligent transport systems: automatic vehicle location, automatic passenger counters and fare collection. It is community governed by the TIDES Project and builds on research from the Transit Cooperative Research Program report on improving access to transit ITS data, without being endorsed by TCRP. Coverage: table schemas for vehicle locations, passenger events, fare transactions, stop visits, trips performed, station activities, vehicles, train cars, devices and operators, with a summary process linking raw AVL, APC and fare records to stops, trips and vehicles. Format and access: JSON table schemas compatible with the Frictionless table schema, a tides-datapackage-profile for datapackage.json metadata, templates and sample data folders, validation tools and generated documentation on GitHub and tides-transit.org; free. Licence: the specification, documentation and sample data are CC-BY-4.0 and the code is Apache-2.0 (LICENSES file). Caveats: TIDES is a format, not a dataset, and agencies must convert their vendor data; adoption and the sample data on the resources page were not checked. Simulation uses: standardised observed ridership, loads, speed and delay for calibrating transit models in capacity planning, network flow and digital twin work. Related records: GTFS (data-gtfs-specification) supplies the schedules TIDES records refer to, and TODS (data-tods-transit-operational-data-standard) covers the planned operational side such as runs and blocks.
